_comment: Layer 1 of the bias detector: pattern-matched phrasing in the JD itself. Layer 2 (impact simulation, in bias_detector.py) measures how many real candidates each hard requirement actually excludes — that layer is the one that produces evidence rather than opinion. `pattern` is a regex applied case-insensitively with word boundaries.

gender_coded.label: Gender-coded language
gender_coded.why: Research on job adverts finds aggressive, competitive phrasing measurably reduces application rates from women.

age_coded.label: Age-coded language
age_coded.why: Signals a preference for younger applicants, which is both exclusionary and in many jurisdictions unlawful.

exclusionary.label: Exclusionary requirements
exclusionary.why: Screens out qualified candidates on grounds unrelated to the ability to do the job.

terms.suggestion: remove, or state that equipment is provided

ableist.label: Ableist phrasing
ableist.why: Physical framing of work that is not physically demanding excludes disabled applicants for no reason.

terms.pattern: must be able to stand|able to lift|physically fit
terms.suggestion: remove unless genuinely essential to the role

elitist.label: Credential elitism
elitist.why: Institution filters correlate with socioeconomic background far more than with engineering ability.

narrow_phrasing.label: Overly narrow requirements
narrow_phrasing.why: Hard thresholds and long mandatory tool lists exclude candidates who could do the job well. Layer 2 measures the real cost against this applicant pool.

terms.suggestion: state the capability needed rather than a duration

_intern_note: When a role matches intern_role_markers AND states a multi-year experience threshold, that contradiction is escalated to critical severity — it is the single most common way an internship advert accidentally excludes its entire intended audience.
